images.filename: Postcards signed Sara, London, to (Ernst Filsinger), New York City, July 24, 1927 - DPLA - f553e8721478d9607b34fb45ea12b204 (page 1).jpg
images.caption: Postcard pictures of the Keats Parlor and the Girometti Medallion at the John Keats House. Includes envelope. Transcription: 46 Grosvenor St. London W.1 July 24, '27 My darling, this room moved me more than anything else that I have seen. I longed to have you see it too. To-day we drove out the Stoke Poges Church where [Thomas] Gray is buried and about which he wrote his poem. From there we went to Eton and saw the fine old buildings of the college. The boys, dressed for Sunday, were adorable. They are the blue bloods of England, you know. Then we had a hasty glance at Windsor (the apartments were not open and I should have been too tired to go in anyway) and passed Runnymede on our way home. I am loving it all tremendously! I send you many kisses. Sara.

images.caption:
1-3 Willow Road, Hampstead (1940) by Ernő Goldfinger.  
Number 2 (the middle house) was Ernő Goldfinger's own house for many years.  It's now owned by the National Trust, and they do tours for visitors on Saturday afternoons (and possibly other times).  It's well worth a visit - the interior is done with great concern for materials and attention to detail.  It's very successful, and much less austere and difficult than you might imagine.  Likewise, you really need to see the outside of the house at close quarters to fully appreciate it - I particularly liked the wood and translucent glass front door and hall area.  

There's also an interesting range of modern art acquired by Goldfinger on display in the house.
